entities.summary:
Rhun ab Arthgal was a ninth-century King of Strathclyde, whose reign was marked by the capture of the fortress of Alt Clut by Vikings in 870, leading to the eventual slaying of Arthgal at the behest of Causantín mac Cináeda, King of the Picts, in 872. This event had significant repercussions on the political landscape of Strathclyde and the broader region. Rhun ab Arthgal's own fate remains shrouded in mystery, with the circumstances of his death unknown.

Rhun ab Arthgal was a member of the royal family of Strathclyde, succeeding his father Arthgal ap Dyfnwal as king after his father's death. The exact nature of his relationship with his family and the extent of his authority are not well-documented.

The Viking invasion of Alt Clut in 870 had far-reaching consequences, leading to the eventual collapse of the Strathclyde kingdom. The event also marked a significant turning point in the history of the region, as it led to the rise of the Pictish kingdom and the eventual unification of Scotland.

Rhun ab Arthgal's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting the tumultuous nature of his reign. His death at the hands of Causantín mac Cináeda marked the beginning of a new era in Strathclyde, one characterized by turmoil and upheaval.

The story of Rhun ab Arthgal serves as a poignant reminder of the fragility of power and the enduring legacy of the past.
